general.title: Shopproof
general.description: EU rules for the countries you sell to

overview.disclaimer: Technical information to help shops comply. Not legal advice.
overview.loadFailed: The rules could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
overview.notYet: The rules list that ships with the plugin is missing. Reinstall the plugin, or press "Check for rule updates now".
overview.countriesHint: Choose the countries you sell to under Extensions > My extensions > Shopproof EU Compliance > Configure. EU-wide rules are always shown.
overview.versionBundled: Rules version {version}, shipped with the plugin.
overview.autoOff: Shopproof works without contacting any server. To get rule changes as they are published, press "Check for rule updates now" or turn on "Download rule updates once a day" in the plugin settings. The download goes to the Shopproof rules service and sends no shop, customer or personal data.
overview.autoOn: Rule updates are downloaded once a day from the Shopproof rules service. You can turn this off in the plugin settings.
overview.refresh_updated: Rules checked. The list below is the newest version.
overview.refresh_failed: The rules service could not be reached. The rules you already have stay in place; try again later.

withdrawal.listIntro: Every request sent through Shopware's withdrawal button, kept in this shop's database so you can show when it arrived. Shopproof never receives it.
withdrawal.searchLabel: Search by email, name or order number
withdrawal.listFailed: The withdrawal requests could not be loaded. Your user needs the right to view orders.
withdrawal.failedRecords: {count} withdrawal request could not be recorded; check the log and the Shopware emails. | {count} withdrawal requests could not be recorded; check the log and the Shopware emails.
withdrawal.failedHelp: Shopware still sent its emails, so the shopper got a confirmation, but the request is missing from the list below. Find it in the emails Shopware sent to the shop and in var/log (search for "Shopproof could not record"), and keep a copy.
withdrawal.deliveredHelp: The day the customer received the goods (the last item). Without it, the day Shopware marked the delivery as shipped stands in, which can only say "in time" or "check".
withdrawal.notEmailed: No email was sent (the setting is off, or the shop has no email address or template for this storefront).
withdrawal.statusFailed: The status could not be saved. Try again.
withdrawal.confirmStatus: Save this status? The customer gets an email about it, unless status emails are off in the settings.

clock.late: Late by {days} day: window ended {date} | Late by {days} days: window ended {date}
clock.check: Check: may be late, enter the delivery date
clock.unknown: Window unknown: enter the delivery date
clock.none: No refund clock while the withdrawal is late
clock.overdue: Refund overdue by {days} day (was due {date}) | Refund overdue by {days} days (was due {date})
clock.due: Refund due by {date} ({days} day left) | Refund due by {date} ({days} days left)
clock.insideOrder: In time: window ends {date} (14 days from the order, as for services)
clock.performed: Check: the service was fully provided before the withdrawal, after the early start request, so the right may have ended (Art. 16(a))
clock.digital: Check: digital content, and the customer agreed at checkout that the download may start early and that the right then ends. If the download started before the withdrawal, the right may have ended (Art. 16(m))
clock.exempt: Check: dated bookings only (leisure, travel and the like), usually no right of withdrawal (Art. 16(l))
clock.noneRight: No refund clock while the right of withdrawal may not apply

owed.no_consent: Service: the customer pays nothing for what was provided, because there is no early start request (Art. 14(4))
owed.not_started: Service: not started when the withdrawal arrived, nothing owed
owed.days: Service: {days} of {of} days provided, the customer pays {owed}, refund {refund}
owed.share: Service: {share} % provided, the customer pays {owed}, refund {refund}
owed.unknown: Service: enter the service dates or the part provided on the order (Custom fields, Shopproof) to see what the customer pays

clock.help: Technical help, not legal advice. The window is 14 days (or your longer period) from delivery and runs to Monday when it ends on a weekend; public holidays can extend it too. The refund is due 14 days after the withdrawal arrived. For services, the window counts from the order, and with the early start request the customer pays for the part provided.

proof.title: Proof log
proof.intro: A dated record of what your shop showed and which withdrawals it received, kept in your shop's own database. Each entry is chained to the one before by a SHA-256 hash, so a changed or deleted entry shows up when you check the chain. It holds no customer names, email addresses or order numbers. A snapshot is recorded once a day.
proof.unavailable: The proof log table is missing. Update or reinstall the plugin.
proof.loadFailed: The proof log could not be loaded.
proof.none: No entries yet. The first snapshot is recorded within a day, or press "Record a snapshot now".
proof.retention: Entries are kept for {days} days (plugin settings, Proof log).
proof.retentionAll: All entries are kept (plugin settings, Proof log).
proof.verifyBroken: Chain broken at entry {id}, after {count} intact entries. An entry was changed or deleted.

returns.title: Returns tool
returns.intro: Shopproof can send each new withdrawal to your returns tool or automation as signed JSON, and add a link to your returns portal to the customer's receipt. Set the addresses in the Shopproof settings (Returns tool card).
returns.on: On: each new withdrawal is sent to your returns tool.
returns.off: Off: no webhook address is set.
returns.secretHelp: Paste this into your returns tool. Each request carries the header X-Shopproof-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<signature>. The signature is the HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of the time, a dot and the request body, keyed with this secret. Keep the secret private.
returns.renewed: New secret made. Paste it into your returns tool, since the old one no longer works.
returns.testOk: Your returns tool accepted the test (status {code}).
returns.testRefused: Your returns tool refused the test with status {code}. Check the address and the secret there.
returns.testUnreachable: Your returns tool could not be reached. Check the address.

delivery.retrying: Returns tool: not accepted {time} (status {code}). Shopproof will try again.
delivery.failed: Returns tool: gave up {time} (status {code}). Please create the return by hand.

notes.unitPrices_off: These products look sold by weight or volume (for example "500 g" in the name), but have no content and unit set, so Shopware shows no unit price. Open the product, Specifications, Measures and packaging:
notes.depositTypes_off: These lines of "Your deposit types" in the plugin settings are not used. Write them like "de-single | Einweg | 0.25 | single | DE":
notes.checkoutPolicyPages_off: These checkout boxes you chose do not show, because their page is not set in Settings > Basic information:
notes.box_withdrawal: I have read the withdrawal policy (revocation page)
notes.box_privacy: I have read the privacy notice (privacy page)
notes.disputeBoard_off: Your dispute resolution statement names no arbitration board yet. Enter its name in the plugin settings.
notes.disputeStatement_ok: Your dispute resolution statement is on your terms or imprint page
notes.disputeStatement_off: Paste your dispute resolution statement into your terms and imprint pages (Content > Shopping Experiences), or tick that you did in the plugin settings.
notes.disputeIntro: Your dispute resolution statement, to paste in the language of each page:
notes.policyPage_off: Withdrawal policy: not checked, because no revocation page is set in Settings > Basic information. Set it, and Shopproof compares it with your withdrawal period and shop email.
notes.policyText_off: Withdrawal policy: not checked, because your revocation page has almost no text. If it is filled in another way, compare the period and the email address yourself.
notes.policyPeriod_ok: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page says {detail} days, the same as the withdrawal period in the plugin settings
notes.policyPeriodDifferent_off: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page says {detail} days, but the withdrawal period in the plugin settings is different. Change one of them so they match.
notes.policyPeriodMonths_off: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page gives the period in months, so Shopproof cannot compare it. Check that it is the same as the withdrawal period in the plugin settings.
notes.policyPeriodMany_off: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page names more than one period ({detail} days). Check that the withdrawal period in the plugin settings is the right one.
notes.policyPeriodNone_off: Withdrawal policy: no withdrawal period found on your revocation page. Check it yourself.
notes.policyEmail_ok: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page names your shop email
notes.policyEmailDifferent_off: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page names {detail}, not the shop email in Settings > Basic information. Check that customers who write to that address reach you.
notes.policyEmailUnsure_off: Withdrawal policy: your revocation page names {detail}, but no shop email is set in Settings > Basic information, so Shopproof cannot compare it.
notes.policyEmailNone_off: Withdrawal policy: no email address found on your revocation page. Check that it tells customers how to reach you.
notes.where: Change these in Settings > Extensions > Shopproof > Configure (cards Price notes, Bottle deposit, Cart and checkout, Dispute resolution statement). Technical help, not legal advice.

bulk.title: Safety details for many products at once
bulk.intro: Fill in the product safety details of many products in a spreadsheet, with Shopware's own Import/Export:
bulk.step1: Open Settings > Import/Export, tab Export, and export with the profile "Shopproof: product safety". Tick "Export product variants" if your variants have their own details.
bulk.step2: Fill in the columns in the file. Leave the product_number column as it is. Hazard pictograms keep the form of the export, for example ["GHS02","GHS07"].
bulk.step3: Import the file with the same profile, tab Import. Products are matched by product number, and an empty cell leaves the value as it is. A row with an unknown number is not imported: Shopware then reports the import as failed and offers a file with those rows, while the other rows are saved.
bulk.manufacturers: Most products take their details from their manufacturer. The profile "Shopproof: manufacturer safety details" works the same way for manufacturers, matched by the id column.
bulk.bulkEdit: To give a few products the same details, select them in Catalogues > Products, choose Bulk edit and fill in "Shopproof: product safety (GPSR)" under Custom fields.

placement.title: Check where the withdrawal link appears
placement.intro: Here you see your shop pages as shoppers see them, on a computer and on a phone. The withdrawal button has a blue frame, and anything that covers your theme's content has a red dashed frame. Click around your shop in the preview and each page is checked again. The check runs in your browser and nothing leaves your shop; only the number of pages that passed is saved.
placement.loadFailed: The shop pages for the check could not be loaded. Reload this page to try again.
placement.noChannel: No active storefront with a domain was found, so there is nothing to check.
placement.otherOrigin: {names}: no storefront domain uses the address this admin is open on, so your browser may not show these pages here and they count as not checked. Open the admin on the storefront's own domain, or add that domain to the storefront, to check them.
placement.open: Open this page in a new tab
placement.blocked: We could not show this page in the preview. The admin and the shop may be on different web addresses, a security setting on the server may block previews, or the page sent you to another site. Open the page in a new tab and check it yourself.
placement.sweeping: Checking your pages on a computer and a phone...
placement.last: Last check {date}: {pass} passed, {warn} to look at, {fail} with a problem, {skipped} not checked.
placement.footnote: Technical help, not legal advice. The cookie banner can show as a floating element until you close it in the preview. Then choose the page again to check it once more.

found.fail: No withdrawal button on this page. Shoppers must find it on every page, for example in the footer.
found.skip: No withdrawal button on this page, which is fine here.

visible.pass: Shoppers see it without opening anything.
visible.warn: At this screen width the button is hidden {areas}, for example in a closed menu. Make sure it is also visible somewhere else, such as the footer.

clear.warn: Something covers one of the buttons: {items}.
clear.fail: Something covers the button: {items}. Shoppers cannot reach it.

contrast.pass: Text contrast {value}:1 (the accessibility standard asks for at least 4.5:1).
contrast.warn: The button is hard to read: text contrast is only {value}:1, and the accessibility standard (WCAG 2.2 AA) asks for 4.5:1. Choose other button colours in your theme.
contrast.skip: Contrast not measured: an image or gradient sits behind the text.

floating.pass: Nothing floats over your theme's content.
floating.warn: Something floats over your theme's content: {items}. This does not come from Shopproof. It comes from your theme or another extension.

others.warn: We found another withdrawal button: {items}. Shoppers should see only one. Turn off the button in the other extension.

cancel.title: Cancellations
cancel.intro: Cancellations customers sent on your cancel page (Settings > Extensions > Shopproof, "Cancel button"). Each customer got a confirmation email with the date and time of receipt, and your shop email got a copy.
cancel.failed: The cancellations could not be loaded.

cancel.next: End the contract (for a subscription, in your subscriptions app), tell the customer the end date if they chose the earliest possible date, and mark the cancellation as done. Technical help, not legal advice.
